verdict: SHIP, scoped -- and strike correction 3. All three pre-registered SHIP conjuncts were met and independently reproduced by this review (tooling worked, unlike Q016's reviewer): Round 1 design-time member resolution 0 diagnostics/1203ms with the target record SampleNs.Person provably absent from every reference path (precondition grep reproduced clean); Round 2 live 'email' edit picked up via FileSystemWatcher+Invalidate() 0 diagnostics/40ms with no rebuild; Round 3 the independent, separately-compiled RuntimeConsumer read name/age via the erased members matching direct field access (agreement true/true, exit 0). Myriad.Core.dll was already built and 01-design's reproduction block includes the dotnet build -c Release step, so no reproducibility gap. KILL is out (Myriad.Core.Ast loaded and ran inside the design-time host; erased syntactic-only members were accepted by FCS with the target type absent); REVISE's trigger (runtime half has an unanticipated gap) did not fire; NULL is out (the Myriad.Core.Ast composition plus the explicit design-time/runtime decoupling proof is more than a bare sample-file re-tread). This is genuinely new ground in either thread: the first erased provider, the first to call Myriad's own parser from inside a provider, the first design-time member visibility for a type compiled nowhere reachable, and it sidesteps Q006's wall exactly as claimed (never asks FCS to resolve the record, self-parses and erases to obj) WITHOUT touching the Assembly.LoadFrom file-lock that dead-ended Q016-18 (no satellite DLL, no lock; the live edit just works). But five things travel with the SHIP and matter more than the label. (1) The write-up's biggest 'found by running' correction does NOT reproduce: removing assemblyReplacementMap as a controlled single-variable change (addDefaultProbingLocation left in) leaves all three rounds passing identically, including a clean full dotnet build of RuntimeConsumer and its runtime run -- the claimed FS0074 'must add a reference to assembly MyriadPreview.DesignTime' never appears in any path (parse-and-check, compile-and-emit, or runtime). The map is present and harmless but not load-bearing for an all-obj erased provider; correction 3's 'general finding for this lineage' is a post-hoc misattribution and should be struck. (2) The win is design-time member NAMES, not typed IntelliSense -- every member is obj, so a real editor shows p.name : obj; that ceiling is inherent to the erasure choice, not a tuning gap. (3) It is a parallel Fields<file,name> preview mechanism the user points at a source path (an absolute literal -- __SOURCE_DIRECTORY__ concatenation is rejected in that position), NOT Myriad's [<Lenses>]-on-the-record usage shape restored to the IDE; it sidesteps Q006's wall by not being the thing behind it, so it must not be cited as 'closes Myriad's IDE-invisibility gap'. (4) Round 3 in isolation proves only that reflection works (getterCode is literally o.GetType().GetProperty(f).GetValue(o), a trivial echo indistinguishable from a hand-written helper -- the Q001/Q016 structural-echo trap); the genuine capability is entirely in Rounds 1-2. (5) FSharpChecker-as-library never a real Ionide host, toy flat record, and the erased-sample-file mechanism itself is the ~15-year-old FSharp.Data/JsonProvider pattern (novel to this repo's lineage and the Myriad.Core composition, not new provider machinery). Beyond reproduction the review tested four shapes the executor never did, all degrading gracefully but cheaply because everything is obj: a nested/non-primitive record field round-trips (trivially, via obj cast); a missing record name and a non-record type both surface as clean FS3033 diagnostics naming the record (the 'zero fields' branch is dead code since extractRecords only yields records); and a malformed source file throws a ParseException surfaced as FS3033 with full parse diagnostics and no host hang. The 0.8.6.0 version string is confirmed to be the root Directory.Build.props VersionPrefix leaking via directory-scoped auto-import (DesignTime dll assembly version is 0.8.6.0), correct and masking nothing. Top follow-ups: type the members (primitive types are resolvable, but a field typed by the same uncompiled file walks back toward Q006's wall -- the real open question); strike/downgrade correction 3; a real-IDE host test; and a real Myriad generator shape (Lenses copy-and-update) rather than a flat read-only record.
